{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>''[&hellip;]'' to this day one occasionally sees this script used in military contexts with little attention paid to its sinister origins. Military bunkers on Storinal and Hanod, New Republic task forces, and even a few Ordnance/Regional Depot worlds such as Ord Dalet were identified by Common Sith letters.|Doctor Milanda Vorgan, "The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic"|<ref name="Written" />}}
'''Hanod''' was a terrestrial astronomical object<ref name="Written" /> located in the [[Hanod system/Legends|Hanod system]], a part of the [[Corva sector/Legends|Corva sector]]<ref name="EAOC" /> in the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] portion of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" /> At some point by [[38 ABY]], military bunkers on Hanod were identified by letters from the ancient [[Common Sith]] [[Writing/Legends|writing system]], a fact which was noted by the [[Xenolinguist/Legends|xenolinguist]] [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Milanda Vorgan]] in<ref name="Written" /> her<ref name="TT">{{WEGCite|story=Erasing All Traces|book=The Last Command Sourcebook}}</ref> publication "[[The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic]]."<ref name="Written" />

==Behind the scenes==
Hanod was introduced in the article "[[The Written Word]]," which was authored by [[John Hazlett]] and published on [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] on [[March 5]], [[2010]].<ref name="Written" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Hanod [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore Hanod itself, in grid square P-3.<ref name="TEA" /> Although the entry for the system in the [[2008]] ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' claims that it was situated in the [[Trans-Hydian/Legends|Borderland Regions]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|14|Hanod system}}</ref> that placement was overridden by ''The Essential Atlas'', which established that the region did not, in fact, intersect square P-3.<ref name="TEA" />
